title: Additivity of the Frobenius traces along an open–closed decomposition
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $X_0$ be a
separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, let $i_0:Z_0\hookrightarrow X_0$
be a closed immersion with complementary open immersion
$j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow X_0$, and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$,
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be their base changes to $k$. Let
$(K,\varphi)\in D^b_{ctf,\mathrm W}(X,A)$ be a strict Weil complex
of [def-trf-strict-weil-complex].

1. For $h\in\{i,j\}$ with source $W\in\{Z,U\}$, one has
$h\,g_W=g_X\,h$, and the composite
$$
h^*\varphi:\;
Lg_W^*Lh^*K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Lh^*Lg_X^*K
\xrightarrow{\ Lh^*\varphi\ }Lh^*K
$$
of the canonical pullback identification with $Lh^*\varphi$ makes
$(Lh^*K,h^*\varphi)$ a strict Weil complex on $W$; its iterates of
[def-trf-iterated-weil-map] are
$(h^*\varphi)^{[m]}=Lh^*\varphi^{[m]}\circ c_{h,m}$, with
$c_{h,m}:Lg_W^{m*}Lh^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*Lg_X^{m*}$ the canonical
identification.
1. For every $m\geq1$, with $F_{c,-}^{\,m}$ the global geometric
Frobenius operators of [def-trf-frobenius-operators] for these
Weil structures,
$$
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,K}^{\,m}\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K)\bigr)
=
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,j^*K}^{\,m}\mid R\Gamma_c(U,j^*K)\bigr)
+
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,i^*K}^{\,m}\mid R\Gamma_c(Z,i^*K)\bigr)
$$
in $A$. These are categorical traces of perfect complexes in the
sense of [def-trf-categorical-trace]; no trace of an individual
cohomology module occurs.
1. *(Frobenius coefficient morphisms.)* Let instead
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ carry an arbitrary Frobenius coefficient
morphism $\psi:L\Phi_X^*K\to K$ of
[def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism], with no Weil structure and no
invertibility. For $h\in\{i,j\}$ with source $W$ one has
$h\,\Phi_W=\Phi_X\,h$, the composite
$h^*\psi:L\Phi_W^*Lh^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*L\Phi_X^*K
\xrightarrow{Lh^*\psi}Lh^*K$ is a Frobenius coefficient morphism on
$W$ with iterates $(h^*\psi)_m=Lh^*\psi_m\circ c'_{h,m}$, where
$c'_{h,m}:L\Phi_W^{m*}Lh^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*L\Phi_X^{m*}$ is the
canonical identification, and for every $m\geq1$ the global operators
$F_{c,m}$ of [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] satisfy
$$
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,m}(\psi)\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K)\bigr)
=
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,m}(j^*\psi)\mid R\Gamma_c(U,j^*K)\bigr)
+
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,m}(i^*\psi)\mid R\Gamma_c(Z,i^*K)\bigr).
$$

The proof below uses the Weil maps only as morphisms: the
invertibility of $\varphi$ is used only to stay inside the category
$D^b_{ctf,\mathrm W}$ on which $F_{c,-}^{\,m}$ is defined.

proof.text: Restricted structures and iterates. A finite affine cover of $X$ by finitely generated $k$-algebras has Noetherian underlying spaces by [lem-sfb-finite-type-noetherian-spectrum]. Restricting an ascending chain of opens to this finite cover proves stabilization on $X$. By [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets], every open is quasi-compact, and [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type] makes $j$ finite type. The closed immersion $i$ is locally a quotient map of rings, hence finite type. Thus $i,j$ are separated finite-type maps and their sources are separated finite type over $k$. Apply [thm-sf-ctf-stability](i) to obtain $Lh^*K\in D^b_{ctf}(W,A)$. The equality $hg_W=g_Xh$ follows from their fibre-product definitions. The open square is Cartesian by [lem-trf-frobenius-open-square]; the closed Galois square is Cartesian since the scalar automorphism preserves the defining ideal of $Z_0\times_{k_0}k$. The canonical pullback identification followed by $Lh^*\varphi$ is an isomorphism, giving the structure of [def-trf-strict-weil-complex]. Apply [lem-trf-pullback-coefficient-iterate-coherence] with $(t,u)=(g_X,\varphi)$ to the product of [def-trf-iterated-weil-map]: its conclusion is exactly $(h^*\varphi)^{[m]}=Lh^*\varphi^{[m]}\circ c_{h,m}$. For $t=\Phi_X$, naturality of the scheme Frobenius [def-trf-scheme-frobenius] gives $h\Phi_W=\Phi_Xh$; applying the same lemma to the recursion of [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] proves the stated formula for $h^*\psi$.

Construct the localization filtration before taking derived compact cohomology. By [lem-trf-localization-filtered-section-exchange], $S_X(K)$ is the actual two-step filtered derived object represented by $F^0C=C$, $F^1C=j_!j^*C$, $F^2C=0$, with total $K$ and graded objects $j_!j^*K$, $Ri_*i^*K$. The open is quasi-compact by Step 1. The lemma identifies its underlying triangle with the specified localization triangle of [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages]. Fix $t=g_X^m$, $u=\varphi^{[m]}$. The same lemma gives the filtered comparison $\alpha_t:Lt^*S_X(K)\simeq S_X(Lt^*K)$ and the actual filtered morphism $\widetilde u=S_X(u)\circ\alpha_t$. Its total map is $u$; its graded maps are $j_!(j^*\varphi)^{[m]}\circ b_t$ and $Ri_*(i^*\varphi)^{[m]}\circ e_t$, using Step 1. In particular the closed component is the induced quotient map with its specified adjunction mate; it is not an arbitrarily completed triangle morphism.

source.place: Step 2; extracted filtered section and graded-mate identification

proof.text:
Apply filtered compact cohomology. The two sheaf-localization pieces are in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ by [thm-sf-ctf-stability](iii),(iv) applied to $i,j$ and the restrictions of Step 1. Thus all compact-support comparisons below remain on their stated finite-Tor constructible domains. By [lem-trf-filtered-derived-operation-lifts], $R\Gamma_c(X,-)=\operatorname{Fib}_sRa_{X!}$ has a filtered lift: use a compactification $a_X=pj$, which exists by [thm-nagata-compactification] since $a_X$ is separated finite type and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is affine, hence qcqs, to form $R^Fp_*j_!^F$ and then the exact point fibre functor of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], with compact cohomology as in [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. The compact base-change map along $g_X^m$ over $g_s^m$ has a filtered lift $\widetilde\beta_t$ as well, because it is the canonical exchange built from the sheaf-derived adjunction maps. On the point fibre the constant-coefficient identification removes the pullback by $g_s^m$. Consequently
$\widetilde E=R\Gamma_c^F(X,\widetilde u)\circ\widetilde\beta_t$
is an endomorphism of $R\Gamma_c^F(X,S_X(K))$ in $DF^+(A)$. Forgetting the filtration gives
$E_K=R\Gamma_c(X,u)\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}=F_{c,K}^{\,m}$
by [lem-trf-frobenius-operator-compact-description]. Associated graded gives the same composite on the two pieces, with the two graded coefficient maps found in Step 2; this follows from the associated-graded compatibility of both functors and transformations in the filtered-lift lemma. This constructs the filtered origin required for trace additivity. It does not infer that origin from the existence of a commuting triple in the ordinary derived category.

Identify the two graded operators. For $h=j,i$, use $\lambda_h:R\Gamma_c(X,Rh_!N)\simeq R\Gamma_c(W,N)$ from [prop-functor-package](3). For $i$, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] justify $Ri_!=Ri_*$. Let $b_{t,h}$ be the open exchange or closed mate specified in Step 2. Apply the compact-support vertical-pasting equation in the statement of [lem-trf-filtered-derived-operation-lifts] to $W\to X\to s$ over $g_W^m,g_X^m,g_s^m$. Both inner squares are Cartesian by Step 1. After point evaluation the equation is
$$\lambda_{h,Lt_W^*N}R\Gamma_c(X,b_{t,h})\beta_{t,Rh_!N}=\beta_{t_W,N}\lambda_{h,N}.$$
The cited statement covers the actual compactification-derived exchanges, their composition identifications and filtered lifts, and permits scheme maps not linear over $k$. It therefore supplies precisely the compatibility previously computed inline. Naturality in $N$, Step 1 and [lem-trf-frobenius-operator-compact-description] identify the two graded maps of $\widetilde E$ through $\lambda_j,\lambda_i$ with $F_{c,j^*K}^{\,m}$ and $F_{c,i^*K}^{\,m}$.

source.place: Step 4; existing compact-support vertical-pasting lemma replaces hidden argument

proof.text: Take traces. By [prop-trf-compact-support-perfectness], the total compact complex and the two complexes on $U,Z$ have bounded finite cohomology. To verify perfectness without confusing the two uses of $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$, apply [thm-sf-ctf-stability](iv) to the three structure maps: each $Ra_{W!}Lh^*K$ belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(s,A)$ (and similarly for $W=X$). By [fix-lem-finite-tor-perfect], its derived stalk at $\operatorname{id}_s$ is a bounded finite free $A$-complex. That stalk is the exact point evaluation defining $R\Gamma_c$ in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], so all three compact complexes are perfect in the sense of [def-trf-categorical-trace]. The pullback finite-Tor and constructibility hypotheses were checked in Step 1, and all three structure maps are separated finite type. Hence the two-graded-piece object of Step 3 is in the bounded filtered category with perfect total and graded pieces, and its underlying localization triangle satisfies exactly the filtered-origin hypothesis of [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws](2). That law gives $\operatorname{tr}_A(E_K)=\operatorname{tr}_A(\operatorname{gr}^1\widetilde E)+\operatorname{tr}_A(\operatorname{gr}^0\widetilde E)$. Conjugacy invariance, item (1) of the same node, and Step 4 give the identity in clause 2. Every trace is taken on the whole perfect complex.

Noninvertible Frobenius coefficient morphisms: geometry. Set $t=\Phi_X^m$ and $u=\psi_m$. Step 1 already supplies the restriction and iterate formulas, and [lem-trf-frobenius-open-square] makes the open square Cartesian. For $T=X,Z$, the affine formula of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius] gives $F_T^{(q)}=g_\sigma\Phi_T$: on $A_0\otimes_{k_0}k$, both sides send $a\otimes b$ to $a^q\otimes b^q$. By [lem-pur-absolute-frobenius-universal-homeomorphism], absolute $q$-power Frobenius is a universal homeomorphism. Its composite with the inverse scalar automorphism is also a universal homeomorphism, since after any base change both factors are homeomorphisms. Thus each $\Phi_T^m$ is a universal homeomorphism. Finiteness follows from [lem-trf-scheme-frobenius-finite-radicial] and induction using [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition], also for $T=U$; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] makes all three iterates proper.

The closed square may be non-Cartesian. By [lem-trf-proetale-topological-invariance], the inverse/direct image adjunctions for $t=\Phi_X^m$ and $t_Z=\Phi_Z^m$ are equivalences of topoi. Their equivalences extend to constant-$A$ modules by transporting the action, and are exact since equivalences preserve kernels and cokernels. They compute the derived functors of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Apply [lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences] with $L=L'=Li^*$, $R=R'=Ri_*$, $G=Lt^*$, and $G'=Lt_Z^*$. The natural isomorphism $\theta:Li^*Lt^*\simeq Lt_Z^*Li^*$ is the canonical comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] for $ti=it_Z$. Here $G$ is an equivalence and $G'$ is fully faithful, exactly the lemma's hypotheses. Its mate is $e_{t,i}:Lt^*Ri_*\to Ri_*Lt_Z^*$, by the unit--square--counit definition of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], so it is invertible. Apply [lem-trf-localization-filtered-section-exchange] to obtain $\widetilde u$ with the prescribed quotient map. No inverse of $u$ is used.

The proper-unit compatibility is [lem-trf-proper-unit-localization-composition], with $t=\Phi_X^m$ and the proper restrictions of Step 6. Its $\beta_t$ is the map induced by $K\to Rt_*Lt^*K$, proper coincidence, and $a_Xt=a_X$. By [lem-trf-filtered-derived-operation-lifts] this map and the compact-cohomology operation have filtered lifts. Hence $R\Gamma_c^F(X,\widetilde u)\circ\widetilde\beta_t$ is an actual filtered endomorphism. By [prop-trf-graph-operator] its total map is exactly $F_{c,m}(\psi)$. The equation of the proper-unit lemma, followed by naturality for the restricted coefficient maps of Step 1, identifies its graded maps through $\lambda_j,\lambda_i$ with $F_{c,m}(j^*\psi)$ and $F_{c,m}(i^*\psi)$, again by [prop-trf-graph-operator]. This supplies the unit-pasting argument of the original Step 6 as a separate lemma rather than a claim that ordinary triangle maps admit a filtered lift.

source.place: Step 6, unit-induced compact operator and its graded maps

proof.text: The perfectness argument of Step 5 applies to the same three coefficient complexes, independent of the chosen coefficient morphism. Apply filtered additivity and conjugacy invariance of [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws] to the filtered endomorphism of Step 8. Its total and graded identifications give the equality in clause 3. The construction used the coefficient morphism only by composition and functor action, and imposed no invertibility hypothesis on $\psi$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N6-fd58678a6 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the three new nodes, every cited statement, the unit sk-i-global-additivity, the main-20261015 proposition and its proof, Varshavsky Ex. 5.2.3 (pp. 43-44) and Stacks lemma-derived-pullback-composition (0D6D). (1) The item statement is word for word the main-20261015 text and is unchanged; the noninvertible-psi clause is not weakened. (2) The route follows the unit: a filtered origin, then prop-trf-trace-formal-laws(2) and (1). Blueprint Steps 1-5 are delivery Steps 1-5 and blueprint Step 6 is Steps 6-9. The blueprint used fix-lem-exchanges, which is for k-morphisms only; the delivery uses the vertical-pasting clause of lem-trf-filtered-derived-operation-lifts instead, which allows non-k-linear maps. Every cited statement off the route is declared as a tool use. (3) Step checks: every hypothesis is met. U is quasi-compact (Noetherian argument), j is finite type, ctf stability(i),(iii),(iv) apply, and both inner squares in the Galois case are Cartesian. (g_sigma Phi)^# sends a(x)b to a^q(x)b^q, which is the absolute Frobenius, so Phi^m is a universal homeomorphism; it is also finite and proper on X, Z and U. lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences applies with G=Lt*, G'=Lt_Z*, and its mate has the right direction t*i_*->i_*t_Z*. In Step 8, prop-trf-graph-operator's T_c is the beta_t of the proper-unit lemma. The perfectness check (ctf(iv), finite-tor-perfect at id_s, Fib_s=Gamma(s,-)) is correct. (4) New nodes. iterate-coherence: the types check, the cocycle is coherence of the pullback comparisons, and I checked the iterate formula by induction using naturality of c_1. localization-filtered-section: alpha_t on F^1 needs only the Cartesian open square; the quotient map is an isomorphism by the five lemma and equals the theta-mate (unit compatibility plus termwise epi), so no Cartesian closed square is needed. I tested Z=V(t) in A^1 under Phi, U=X, U=empty and u=0. proper-unit composition: the types check, and both the closed case (double-mate agreement) and the open case (Rt_*j_! = j_!Rt_U*) hold. None of the three duplicates lem-trf-iterated-weil-cocycle, lem-trf-weil-shriek-iterates, lem-trf-invariant-localization-filtered-lift, lem-trf-finite-horizontal-shriek-mate or lem-trf-filtered-derived-operation-lifts, and none restates a clause of the item. B1-B9 hold.
